national_raw_news.title: Meghalaya CM Conrad K. Sangma assures strict action over Shillong violence 10 mins ago 7
national_raw_news.content: The five-day Autumn Session of the Meghalaya Legislative Assembly commenced today, with the recent incident of violence in Shillong emerging as a key concern. Meghalaya Chief Minister Conrad K. Sangma assured strict action against those involved in the August 19 violence that was caused during the black-flag bike rally organised by the Khasi Students’ Union (KSU) in Shillong. He said that the state government has taken strong note of the incident and would leave no stone unturned to bring those responsible to justice. Making a Suo-motu statement in the Assembly, Sangma said 31 vehicles were attacked, 18 people injured and 15 FIRs were registered. Five masked suspects have been identified, with one arrested. A Special Investigation Team (SIT) has been formed to identify and prosecute those responsible. He added that the Meghalaya state government is also working with the Assam authorities to restore normalcy and ensure smooth movement of vehicles and essential commodities between the two states. Meanwhile, Leader of Opposition, Dr. Mukul M. Sangma called for strict action against all non-government actors responsible Several bills were introduced on the first day. These were Meghalaya Forest Authority (Amendment) Bill 2026, Meghalaya Money Lenders and Accredited Loan Providers’ Bill 2026, Meghalaya Right to Public Services (Amendment) Bill 2026, Meghalaya Official Language Bill 2026 along with bills concerning different private universities including the International Open University (Repealing), Khasi Jaintia Presbyterian University, Sister Nivedita University, Mahatma Gandhi University (Amendment), Martin Luther Christian University (Amendment), and Maharashtra Institute of Technology University of Meghalaya (Amendment). The Assembly also paid tribute to 22 departed leaders and conveyed condolences to their bereaved families on the first day. The five-day sitting, which will end on August 28th, will feature three days allocated to government business and two days for private members’ business.
